thought: the paste went on a prince; she could have sold it as royal
line: Ought to call it the prince's paste now. Sell twice as much, I would.

thought: running through the recipe, tickled it was fit for royalty
line: Ash, flour, water, redberries. Good enough for a prince, apparently.

thought: proud of how well the disguise worked
line: Mix a bit of ash in, and nobody knows a prince from a pauper.

thought: stirring and muttering; sure the muttering did it
line: The muttering's what does it. Worked on the prince, didn't it?

thought: wondering idly what became of her paste on the prince
line: Wonder if that prince ever washed my paste off. Shame if he did.

thought: off redberry picking again, a grievance despite the fame
line: A prince wore my paste, and still I'm picking my own redberries.

thought: marvelling at where her little potion ended up
line: A prince's face, and a witch's paste. Who'd have thought it?

thought: she makes pretty things; disguising was a new use
line: I make things pretty, mostly. Making a prince look ordinary was new.

thought: spots the player who carried her paste off for the rescue
line: There's my clever one. Got a prince out under a dab of paste!

thought: offers help for the next rescue, fond
line: Hello, dearie. Any more princes need hiding, you know where I am.

thought: remembers the player carried the paste carefully
line: You carried that paste so careful, dearie. Not a smear wasted.

thought: tells the cauldron about the player, witchy whimsy
line: Aggie told the cauldron all about that one. It bubbled, very pleased.

thought: credits the pair of them, mostly the paste
line: Fooled Lady Keli, the pair of us. Well, mostly my paste.

thought: a witch likes her work used well
line: A witch likes a customer who puts her paste to proper use, dearie.

thought: greets the player by a new pet name
line: Ooh, it's my prince-smuggler! Mind how you go, dearie.

thought: thinks the player understood what a disguise needs
line: You'd make a decent witch, my dear. You know what paste is for.

thought: never got thanked for the royal paste
line: Paste for a prince, and did I get a thank-you? Not from you, dearie.

thought: the paste did the real work, the player only carried it
line: Who got the prince out? My paste. You just carried the pot.

thought: one disguise doesn't make a witch
line: Don't think one disguised prince makes you a witch, dearie.

thought: busy rescuing princes but not saying hello
line: Rescuing princes, and you can't stop to say hello to a witch?

thought: Keli was fooled; Aggie isn't
line: Lady Keli was fooled by my paste, dearie. Aggie isn't fooled by you.

thought: expects the player back wanting paste for every scrape
line: Don't come asking for prince's paste for every scrape you're in.

thought: fame doesn't excuse the fine for rudeness
line: Saved a prince, did you? The fine for cheek is still the fine, dearie.

thought: the player never picked their own redberries
line: I'll bet you never picked a redberry for that paste yourself.

thought: Baba's reputation as a thief is, to Ali, the highest praise
line: Baba, called a thief for selling too well. I could weep with pride.

thought: all that business and the stall is still his alone
line: Still no assistant behind this counter. After all that, my friend!

thought: calls the scheme tourism, proudly
line: Tourism, my friend. Pollnivneach has never been so full of visitors.

thought: hunting new suppliers for the expansion
line: Suppliers! Who in this desert sells blackjacks by the crate?

thought: fond of his partners in Pollnivneach
line: The mayor and I understand each other. Men of business, both of us.

thought: the boy is in hiding, which Ali takes as a mark of talent
line: Hiding, the boy is. The best salesmen always have to hide a while.

thought: grand plans, only missing the goods
line: Expansion, my friend! Fine clothes, runes... I only need a supplier.

thought: his family spreading the trade everywhere
line: Farid at the Exchange, Baba in hiding. My family does get about.

thought: the player went all that way; he calls it tourism
line: My friend! You went all the way to Pollnivneach. A true tourist.

thought: offers a family price to the one who found Baba
line: For the one who found my Baba, a price I give only to family.

thought: would hire the player; the post is still open
line: Behind this counter, my friend, there is still room for one more.

thought: remembers the player bought the disguise without complaint
line: Ah, my best customer! A beard, a headdress, and never a complaint.

thought: the player found the boy where a whole town could not
line: You found the boy when a whole town could not. Remarkable, my friend.

thought: the greatest salesman pays a rare compliment
line: The greatest salesman in the world tips his hat to you, my friend.

thought: the player took the scheme in good part
line: Such a good sport, my friend! Not everyone enjoys a little tourism.

thought: Baba would approve of the player, a fellow seller
line: Baba would like you, my friend. You both know how to disappear.

thought: the player crossed the desert, and paid him for the privilege
line: You crossed the desert for my nephew? And you paid for the beard!

thought: the player was slow to see the business in it
line: Took you a while to see the business in it, my friend. Tourism!

thought: walks past a job and he still has no assistant
line: Still no assistant, and you walk past a perfectly good job, my friend.

thought: wouldn't let the player mind the stall, having seen them bargain
line: I would ask you to mind the stall, but I have seen you bargain.

thought: a tourist who complains disappoints the town
line: A tourist who complains? Pollnivneach would be so disappointed.

thought: the false beard went to the player's head
line: A false beard went to your head, my friend. It happens to tourists.

thought: the player fetched a nephew who needed no fetching
line: You fetched a nephew who did not need fetching. A born customer, you.

thought: offers another relative to find, a wink at the scheme
line: My favourite visitor! Would you care to find another relative?

thought: the dragon gone, he wonders whether Crandor will speak again
line: Crandor without its dragon. I wonder if word will come from it again.

thought: the roof lookouts are pointless now
line: I've had the roof swept. There's nothing up there to watch for now.

thought: the dragon-slayer keeps taking shields
line: Another shield gone to the dragon-slayer. I really must order more.

thought: likes to think his shield helped
line: Elvarg slain, with one of my shields. I like to think it helped.

thought: his father never slept for fear; he will
line: Father never slept a whole night for fear of that dragon. I shall.

thought: pleased his rule about worthy causes proved right
line: Shields for the worthy, I always said, and for once I was right.

thought: Lumbridge has something Varrock lacks
line: Lumbridge has a dragon-slayer now. Varrock has nothing of the sort.

thought: a quiet prayer of thanks, pompously phrased
line: Saradomin be thanked, there is one dragon fewer in the world.

thought: greets the dragon-slayer formally
line: Ah, the slayer of Elvarg! Lumbridge is honoured, my dear.

thought: the shield is theirs whenever they like
line: A shield whenever you like, adventurer. You've more than earned it.

thought: his father's fear is ended at last
line: Father would have given you the whole roof, I expect, for that dragon.

thought: relieved the player proved brave and not reckless
line: Brave and not reckless, after all. I did wonder, about the dragon.

thought: the worthy cause found a worthy bearer
line: That was a truly worthy cause, and you a most worthy bearer.

thought: amazed the dragon fell to someone who passes his door
line: To think Crandor's dragon fell to someone who walks past my door.

thought: fussing about receiving a dragon-slayer properly
line: Hmm, a dragon-slayer in my castle. I must have the good chairs dusted.

thought: the slayer of his father's dragon deserves a blessing
line: By Saradomin, the dragon my father feared is gone. I've you to thank.

thought: slew a dragon, still can't knock
line: Elvarg slain, and you still can't knock? Dragon-slayers, honestly.

thought: keeps coming back for shields
line: Another shield already? One begins to wonder what you do with them.

thought: the castle hears of the dragon daily
line: One dragon, and the castle hears of it daily. Do pace yourself.

thought: worries the player will lead the next dragon home
line: Do try not to lead the next dragon back here, my dear.

thought: father kept lookouts for the dragon; he'd keep one for the player
line: Father posted lookouts for a dragon. I may yet post one for you.

thought: heroics don't excuse muddy boots
line: Slaying dragons is all very well. Wiping one's boots would be better.

thought: his shields aren't for propping doors
line: Dragon-slayer or not, my shields are not for propping doors open.

thought: fusses over whether his shield survived
line: I gave you that shield in good faith. I trust it's still in one piece?

thought: the graveyard is quiet and he's forgotten what that's like
line: Quiet in the graveyard at last. I'd almost forgotten the sound of it.

thought: he used to say good night and get an answer; now nothing
line: Not a moan from the graveyard all week. I keep listening for one.

thought: visitors come to the graves again
line: People visit the graves again. Saradomin be praised for small mercies.

thought: still wary of warlocks after the skull business
line: Skull-stealing warlocks. I still lock the vestry, just in case.

thought: means to write to Urhney with the news
line: Must write to Urhney and tell him. He'll pretend not to care.

thought: holy water left over, nothing to use it on
line: Holy water left over, and no ghost to use it on. Waste not...

thought: swept the paths without looking over his shoulder
line: I swept the graveyard paths this morning without once looking round.

thought: likes to think his 'Avaunt' helped in the end
line: Avaunt worked in the end, I like to think. With a little help.

thought: recognises the one who laid the ghost
line: Ah, the one who laid our ghost to rest! Bless you, traveller.

thought: points the player out as the graveyard's friend
line: There goes the friend of our graveyard. The dead rest easier now.

thought: getting help from Urhney is its own miracle
line: A kind word out of Urhney and a ghost at rest. A miracle, nearly.

thought: keeps the player in his prayers, honestly
line: I mention you in my prayers, traveller. Most evenings, anyway.

thought: the graveyard looks better since
line: The graves look tidier since you came by. Saradomin's work, and yours.

thought: a warlock's mischief undone by a passer-by
line: A warlock's mischief, undone by a passer-by. Saradomin does provide.

thought: admits the player was braver than him
line: You were braver in that graveyard than I ever was, my friend.

thought: offers a blessing whenever wanted
line: If ever you need a blessing, traveller, you know where to find me.

thought: well done with the ghost; now the player's own soul
line: Good work with the ghost. Now, about your own soul...

thought: the player walks boldly past the graveyard now, unlike before
line: You walk past my graveyard so boldly now. It was not always so.

thought: one ghost doesn't make a priest
line: One ghost laid, and you think yourself a priest? It takes more prayer.

thought: no warlock-hunting in his pews
line: No warlock-hunting in my pews, traveller. They're for sitting.

thought: Saradomin saw the good deed and the missed services
line: Saradomin saw what you did for the ghost. He also sees an empty pew.

thought: hopes the player thanked Urhney; nobody ever does
line: I hope you thanked Urhney. Somebody ought to, once in his life.

thought: deflates the player: a ghost is only a lost parishioner
line: Don't look so pleased. A ghost is only a very lost parishioner.

thought: the player handled a stolen skull, which makes him squeamish
line: You carried that skull about by hand? I'd have used tongs.

thought: still can't believe the talk of penguins dressed as sheep
line: Penguins in my field, dressed as sheep. Whatever next?

thought: counted the flock and they're all sheep
line: Counted the flock again. Sheep, every last woolly one of 'em.

thought: sheep don't waddle; he knows his trade
line: Sheep don't waddle. I've farmed long enough to know that much.

thought: The Thing is bad enough without birds
line: The Thing's bad enough without folk adding penguins to it.

thought: imagines what nonsense comes next
line: Penguins on a sheep farm. Next it'll be fish in the onion bed.

thought: he'll worry when a sheep squawks
line: If one of my sheep starts squawking, then I'll worry. Not before.

thought: different folk see different things in a sheep
line: Some folk see a sheep and think birds. I see a sheep and think wool.

thought: the gate's open again; he refuses to blame birds
line: Gate's open again. And don't nobody tell me it was penguins.

thought: grudging: the player meant well
line: You meant well, with your penguins. I'll give you that much.

thought: odd, but shuts the gates
line: Odd sort, you, but you shut my gates. That counts for plenty.

thought: whatever the player saw, the sheep came to no harm
line: Whatever you saw out there, my sheep came to no harm. Much obliged.

thought: decent, even if they hear voices
line: Decent folk, you, even if you do hear voices about birds.

thought: a keen eye, too keen
line: Keen eyes, you've got. See things that aren't there, but keen.

thought: the player frets over his flock more than he does
line: You fret over my sheep more than I do. Wrong way round, but kind.

thought: at least someone watches his field
line: Least you were watching my field. Most folk just tramp through it.

thought: if anyone could spot The Thing, it's this one
line: You'd spot The Thing if anyone would. You spot everything, you do.

thought: sorry to report the sheep are still sheep
line: Back again? The sheep are still sheep, you'll be sorry to hear.

thought: penguins dressed as sheep, and they call him simple
line: Birds in sheep's wool, says you. And folk call farmers simple.

thought: send the bird talk to the chickens
line: Go and tell the chickens about your penguins. They might listen.

thought: Seth Groats has all the birds anyone could want
line: If you're wanting birds, try Seth Groats. He's got loads.

thought: it's sheep, they baa
line: Hearing voices in my field, are you? It's sheep. They baa.

thought: mock-asks which sheep is the spy
line: Which one's the penguin, then? The one looking at you funny?

thought: no poking his sheep for feathers
line: Don't you go poking my sheep for feathers, you scoundrel.

thought: points out the stranger who thinks his ewes have beaks
line: There goes the one who thinks my ewes have beaks.

thought: the prince is home; even the books look happier
line: The prince is home, and the ledgers have never looked so cheerful.

thought: the Emir rests easier, and so does he
line: The Emir rests easier now his son is home. So, I confess, do I.

thought: Osman won't say how it was done
line: Osman says nothing of how it was done. I have stopped asking.

thought: the palace is quiet in the good way again
line: We are a quiet palace again, and a quiet palace is a happy one.

thought: he writes the Emir's thanks for him now
line: I write the Emir's thanks for him now. He tires so very easily.

thought: still checks the prince's rooms out of habit
line: I find myself checking the prince's rooms each morning. Habit.

thought: someone has been at the windows; surely not the rescuer
line: Scrabbling at the windows again. Not our rescuer, I do hope.

thought: the city's true wealth is water, and now its prince too
line: We have water, and now we have our prince. A rich city indeed.

thought: greets the friend of Al Kharid
line: Ah, our friend of Al Kharid! The palace will never forget you.

thought: the Emir is too frail, so Hassan thanks the player for him
line: The Emir is too frail to say it himself, so I shall. Thank you.

thought: water for the rescuer, always
line: Water for you, whenever you wish. It is the least we can offer.

thought: good day on the Emir's behalf
line: On behalf of the Emir, good day to the one who brought his son home.

thought: the player did what a palace couldn't
line: You did what an entire palace could not. We remember such things.

thought: glad to see the rescuer in the streets
line: Our prince's rescuer, walking our streets. I do like to see it.

thought: knew the player could do it; Osman claims he knew first
line: I knew you could get the job done. Osman claims he knew first.

thought: the Emir's gratitude, and his own humbler share
line: Our Emir is forever grateful, and so, in my humbler way, am I.

thought: a friend, yes, but the window still isn't a door
line: A friend of Al Kharid, yes. The windows are still not a door.

thought: rescued the prince but still won't wipe their boots
line: You rescued the prince, and still you will not wipe your boots?

thought: gratitude has no limit, the treasury has
line: Our gratitude is boundless. Our treasury, I must remind you, is not.

thought: no statue for the hero
line: Do not expect a statue. We are a wealthy city, not a foolish one.

thought: welcome, though he'd still count the spoons
line: Welcome as ever, though I would still count the spoons after you.

thought: a rescue doesn't open the kitchens
line: Rescuing a prince does not entitle one to the palace kitchens.

thought: asks the hero to be less heroic indoors
line: Our hero returns. Do try to be a little less heroic indoors.

thought: grateful, truly, but no need to keep reminding them
line: We are grateful, truly. You need not remind us quite so often.

thought: one old recipe nearly killed everyone; back to burnt cakes
line: Nearly got everyone killed with one old recipe. I'll stick to cakes.

thought: his great ancestor's shadow
line: Franizzard Van Lumbcook. Big boots to fill, and I've small feet.

thought: still doesn't know when the Duke's birthday is
line: It was never the Duke's birthday. I still don't know when it is.

thought: a job for life by inheritance; he'd like to earn it
line: A job for life, from an ancestor. I'd like to earn it myself, one day.

thought: checks every recipe now for anything magical
line: I read every recipe twice now, for anything... magical. Just in case.

thought: the guests frozen at a feast he cooked
line: Oh, the guests! Frozen stiff at the table, and over my cooking.

thought: plain cooking from now on
line: Plain cakes from now on. Burnt, I expect, but plain.

thought: the Duke is still speaking to him, somehow
line: Weeellll... the Duke's still speaking to me. That's something.

thought: the player saved the feast and his job
line: The whole feast saved, my friend, and the cook along with it!

thought: without the player that recipe would have finished them
line: Without you, that recipe would have been the end of us all.

thought: even his ancestor never had such help
line: Even my great ancestor never had help like you, my friend.

thought: tested them with a fake birthday; they passed
line: I tested you with a birthday that wasn't. You passed, and then some.

thought: the Culinaromancer is done for, and so nearly were they
line: Ooh, it's you! The Culinaromancer's done for, and so nearly were we.

thought: if he ever becomes a great cook, half the credit is theirs
line: If I'm ever a great cook, my friend, it'll be half your doing.

thought: every guest came out alive
line: Every guest came out of it alive, thanks to you. Every one!

thought: the big cheeses owe the player their lives
line: My friend, the big cheeses owe you their lives. Not that they'll say.

thought: sulks: anyone could have used the wrong recipe
line: Don't look at me like that. Anyone could have used the wrong recipe.

thought: a feast in the player's honour would only burn
line: A feast in your honour? I'd burn it, and then where would we be?

thought: the player saved everyone; he did all the cooking
line: Yes, yes, you saved everyone. Some of us did all the cooking.

thought: suspects the hero wants a seat at the Duke's table
line: Oh, the hero of the feast. Wanting a seat at the Duke's table now?

thought: the player never asked whose birthday it really was
line: You never asked if it was really the Duke's birthday. Trusting sort.

thought: would thank properly but the player would want feeding
line: I'd thank you properly, but you'd only want feeding.

thought: keep away from the old cookbook
line: Mind you don't touch that old cookbook. Look what happened last time.

thought: beat the Culinaromancer, but can they bake
line: You beat the Culinaromancer. Could you make a cake that doesn't burn?

thought: opened the shutters and only light came in
line: Opened the shutters this morning. Nothing came in but the light.

thought: what to do with all that garlic
line: What do I do with all this garlic now? Cook with it, I suppose.

thought: still sleeps with a scarf on, from habit
line: Still sleep with the scarf on. Old habits, that's all it is.

thought: the village is still named after him
line: Still named after him, this village. Somebody ought to see to that.

thought: rereads the legends to be sure it's over
line: Staked, and gone. I've read the legends twice over to be sure.

thought: walked towards the manor, nearly
line: Walked past the manor gate today. Well, near it. Well, towards it.

thought: he always said the Count had to be stopped
line: I always said he had to be stopped. And now he has been.

thought: many failed; then came his hero
line: The legends are full of folk who failed. Not my hero, though.

thought: sees the hero again and thanks them again
line: Oh! It's you again! Have I thanked you today? Thank you!

thought: points out the one who staked the Count
line: Draynor owes that one so much. Staked the Count, they did!

thought: sleeps through the night now
line: I sleep the whole night through now, adventurer. All thanks to you.

thought: knew it on first sight, or hoped it
line: Bold adventurer! I knew it the moment I saw you. Well, I hoped it.

thought: did what the ones in the legends couldn't
line: You did what all the others in the legends never could.

thought: tells everyone about the player; they've stopped listening
line: I tell everyone about you. They've stopped listening, but I tell them.

thought: offers all his garlic
line: If ever you need garlic, adventurer, mine's yours. All of it.

thought: his neck is the most grateful part of him
line: My neck thanks you most of all, brave adventurer. Bless you.

thought: staked a vampyre and still no garlic
line: You staked a vampyre and still go about without garlic? Honestly.

thought: took so long he nearly ran out of garlic
line: Took your time with the Count. I nearly ran out of garlic.

thought: he did all the reading
line: Don't let it go to your head. I did all the reading.

thought: walked into that manor without a care
line: You walked right into that manor without a care. Reckless, I call it.

thought: manor dust on the boots
line: Hero or not, you'll knock the manor dust off before you come in.

thought: never thanked for the warning
line: You never once thanked me for the warning, you know.

thought: some of them were frightened the whole time
line: Don't look so pleased. Some of us were frightened the whole time.

thought: the hero gets the credit, the worrier gets nothing
line: You get called a hero. I get called jumpy. Hardly fair, is it?

thought: thinks of adding wigs to the business, royal custom and all
line: Ned's Handmade Wigs, I could call it. Royal custom, an' all.

thought: same hands make rope and wigs
line: Wigs and rope, both from wool. Same hands, different knots.

thought: his wool sat on royalty; probably itched
line: Never thought old Ned's wool would sit on royalty. Itchy, I'd expect.

thought: a prince escaped in his wig and no rum came of it
line: Prince got clean away in my wig, and not a drop of rum came of it.

thought: proud of the tight work that fooled a kidnapper
line: Lady Keli never looked twice at that wig. Good tight work, that.

thought: if a wig fools a kidnapper, think of his rope
line: If a wool wig can fool a kidnapper, think what my rope could do.

thought: can't wait to brag at the docks
line: A prince in one of me wigs. Wait till I tells 'em down the docks.

thought: wool is wool, whatever it ends up as
line: Wool's wool. Rope one day, a prince's hair the next.

thought: points out the one who smuggled a prince in his wig
line: There goes the one who smuggled a prince out in old Ned's wig.

thought: the player knew where to come for a wig
line: You knew where to come for a wig. Clever, that. Old Ned's the best.

thought: got the prince home under his wool; proud of them both
line: Got that prince home under my wool, didn't you? Proud of us both.

thought: Ned's wool and the player's nerve
line: A prince saved by Ned's wool and your nerve. I likes that.

thought: not many would think of a wig
line: Proper rescuer, you are. Not many'd have thought of a wig.

thought: anything in wool for the player, bar jumpers
line: Anything you want in wool, old Ned's yours. Bar jumpers.

thought: the player has a sailor's nerve
line: You've the nerve for a rescue. Sailor's nerve, I calls it.

thought: the prince's kidnappers were nothing to the monsters he's fought, but well done
line: Kidnappers ain't monsters, but you saw 'em off all the same. Good.

thought: asked for a wig; next it'll be a bonnet
line: Asked old Ned for a wig, did you? Next you'll want a bonnet.

thought: made a wig, but they still won't buy his rope
line: Wigs for princes, aye. But you'll still not buy my rope.

thought: folk will think he's gone soft
line: Folk'll think old Ned's gone soft, making wigs for the likes of you.

thought: sailed the seas and ended up doing hair
line: A wig! I sailed the seas, and you had me doing hair.

thought: no matching beard; he has his pride
line: Don't go asking for a matching beard. Old Ned has his pride.

thought: no tot of rum for the wig
line: Saved a prince with my wool, and never a tot of rum for old Ned.

thought: the player would make a poor prince
line: You'd make a poor prince, you would. Wig'd slip off at the gate.

thought: laughing at his wigs is a mistake monsters have made
line: Laughing at old Ned's wigs? Monsters have tried that, and lost.

thought: the prince is home and he can go back to being ignored
line: Prince Ali is home, and the city has gone back to ignoring me. Good.

thought: sq'irk juice is purely professional
line: Sq'irk juice sharpens the fingers. I take it purely for the work.

thought: the sorceress gives him no more fruit
line: She gives me no more fruit. We had words, once. That is all.

thought: his daughter says nothing of her work, as taught
line: My daughter says nothing of her work. I taught her well.

thought: a rescue without bodies is how it should be done
line: A rescue with no bodies. That is how such things should be done.

thought: keeps a short list for dangerous work
line: I keep a short list for dangerous work. It is shorter than one thinks.

thought: juice before noon, for the fingers
line: Juice before noon? A spymaster must keep his fingers light.

thought: the Menaphites will have heard; let them wonder
line: The Menaphites will have heard of the rescue. Let them wonder how.

thought: formal greeting to someone tested
line: Hello again. You did that job quietly. I have not forgotten.

thought: the player never boasted of the rescue
line: You have not boasted of the rescue in the market. I noticed.

thought: professional work; rare praise
line: Professional work, that rescue. I do not say so often.

thought: Leela has promoted the player
line: Leela has stopped calling you 'the stranger'. That is a promotion.

thought: the player is filed under useful now
line: You are filed under 'useful' now. Few are. Fewer stay there.

thought: not a word about the prince from the player
line: Not one word from you about the prince, all this time. Good.

thought: the player walks past the palace as if they belong; earned
line: You walk past the palace as though you belong. You have earned it.

thought: trusts nobody, distrusts this one a little less
line: I do not trust people. You I distrust a little less.

thought: the prince is rescued; stop looking pleased
line: You again. The prince is rescued; you may stop looking pleased.

thought: a spy is never famous; the player now is
line: A spy is never famous. You, I fear, have become famous.

thought: won't share his sq'irk juice
line: Do not ask me for sq'irk juice. I have barely enough for myself.

thought: hoping to be a spy now? still no
line: If you are hoping to be a spy now, the answer is still no.

thought: the job is done, no song
line: You did the job. Do not make a song of it.

thought: strolling past the palace again
line: Strolling past the palace again. Old habits, or are you lost?

thought: Hassan calls the player a friend; of course he would
line: Hassan calls you a friend of the city. Hassan would.

thought: lucky once; not twice
line: Lucky, that rescue. I would not count on luck twice.

thought: Irena no longer watches the gate
line: Irena has stopped watching the gate. I almost miss her company.

thought: Ana home and already eyeing the dunes
line: Ana is home, and already eyeing the dunes again. That girl!

thought: next time Ana passes she reads the billboard
line: Next time Ana passes, she reads the billboard first. Twice.

thought: the waterskin he kept for the girl can be sold now
line: The waterskin I kept for the girl... I suppose I can sell it now.

thought: quiet gate, happy mother
line: A quiet gate and a happy mother. A warden asks for nothing more.

thought: the desert rarely gives anyone back
line: The desert gave one back. It does not do that often.

thought: Irena smiles at everyone, even the toll
line: Irena smiles at everyone now. Even at the toll.

thought: the toll covers repairs and wages, nothing more
line: Repairs to the gate, wages for my men, and not a coin over.

thought: knows who to thank for Ana
line: Hello again, friend. Irena's girl is home, and I know who to thank.

thought: points out who brought Ana home
line: There goes the one who brought Ana home. My gate salutes them.

thought: walked into the sands and out with a child
line: You walked into the sands and walked out with a child. Remarkable.

thought: a mother sleeps because of the player
line: A mother sleeps at night because of you, friend. No small thing.

thought: sells waterskins to many, tips his hat to few
line: I sell waterskins to many. I tip my hat to very few, friend.

thought: the sands gave the player back, and the girl too
line: The sands gave you back, friend, and brought the girl along too.

thought: still has to see the pass, a little
line: No need for a pass, friend. Well, a little need. Rules are rules.

thought: a rescuer who still pays the toll
line: A rescuer who still pays the toll. You are a credit, friend.

thought: Ana's home; stop looking pleased at his gate
line: Ana is home, friend. You may stop looking so pleased at my gate.

thought: did they read the billboard first? no
line: Brought the girl back, yes. Did you read the billboard first? No.

thought: if Ana runs off again, the player can fetch her
line: If Ana runs off again, you can fetch her. I have a gate to mind.

thought: hero of the desert, still haggles over the toll
line: Hero of the desert, and still you haggle over a small toll.

thought: saving girls is good; so is buying a robe
line: Saving girls in the desert is good work. So is paying for a robe.

thought: the cell's still there; heroes need it too
line: The cell is still there, friend. Heroes have been known to need it.

thought: a hero will want a free drink now
line: A hero at my gate. I suppose you will want a cool drink for nothing.

thought: found one lost girl; now find the end of the queue
line: You found one lost girl, friend. Now find the end of my queue.

thought: fooling a troll Mother at his age, from a coffin
line: Oh dear, oh dear. Fooling a troll Mother at my age, and from a coffin.

thought: if he must lie in a coffin, it'll be good wood
line: Mahogany, that coffin. If I'm to lie in one, it'll be good wood.

thought: drove Mother's band out in his youth; she remembers
line: Drove Mother's band out of those tunnels in my youth. She remembers.

thought: playing dead is harder than it looks
line: Playing dead is harder than it looks. Especially after a big lunch.

thought: has slept in worse places than a coffin
line: I've slept in worse places than a coffin. Entrana's beds, for one.

thought: money doesn't matter once you have plenty
line: Money doesn't matter once you've as much as I have. Remember that.

thought: denies snoring; it was the wood creaking
line: I don't snore. That was the coffin, creaking. Mahogany creaks.

thought: lay so still he nearly fooled himself
line: Lay so still in that box, I nearly fooled myself.

thought: the player would have done well against Mother's lot
line: You'd have done well against Mother's lot. Nearly as well as me.

thought: trusts the player not to tell about the snoring
line: Ah, the young hero! You'd never tell about the snoring, would you?

thought: good to see the player up and about, unlike some
line: Good to see you up and about, my dear. Some of us had to lie in boxes.

thought: the player has the nerve for trolls, as he did once
line: You've the nerve for trolls, I'll give you that. I had it once, too.

thought: the one he'd trust with his coffin
line: Of all the young heroes, you're the one I'd trust with my coffin.

thought: a credit to the new generation, almost to the old
line: A credit to the new generation, you are. Almost a credit to the old.

thought: never laughed about the coffin, to his face
line: You never laughed at me about the coffin. Well, not to my face.

thought: would make a fine sage; learn to snore quietly
line: You'd make a fine sage one day. Learn to snore quietly first.

thought: don't tell the village about the snoring
line: Don't you dare tell the village about the snoring. Not a word.

thought: he was playing dead; the player manages it without trying
line: I was only playing dead. You, I hear, manage it without trying.

thought: stop grinning; anyone would snore in mahogany
line: Less of the grinning, young lad. You'd snore too, in mahogany.

thought: trolls at his age, and the player stood about
line: Trolls, at my age! And you just stood about, I expect.

thought: drove trolls from tunnels; the player would struggle with a cellar
line: I've driven trolls out of tunnels. You'd struggle with a cellar.

thought: a coffin is no excuse to inherit the hat
line: Staring at my hat again? A coffin doesn't mean you inherit it.

thought: the player can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one; Mother could
line: Can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one? Mother could, worse luck.

thought: thinks themselves brave; he lay in a box beside a troll
line: Think yourself brave? I lay in a box beside a troll, young lad.
